slides.kicker: NO HIRING. NO CODING. START TONIGHT.

slides.headline: 1) MAP YOUR WHOLE MARKET IN 10 MINUTES
slides.body: Market research firms charge $3,000 for a competitor analysis. This prompt builds the same output in 10 minutes and costs nothing. Copy-paste prompt: "List the 10 biggest competitors in [your market]. For each: their pricing, top 3 customer complaints from public reviews, and the one gap they all miss. Format as a table."

slides.headline: 2) TURN YOUR IDEA INTO A BUILD PLAN
slides.body: Technical project managers charge $2,500 to scope a software build. This prompt creates the same task breakdown in under 20 minutes. Copy-paste prompt: "My app idea: [one sentence]. Break it into an ordered feature list. For each feature include: complexity rating, which features depend on it, and the exact build sequence for a solo developer."
slides.image_prompt: One hand gripping a marker pointing at a whiteboard showing four numbered boxes connected by arrows (zero text inside any box), a laptop open below on the desk, clean afternoon side-light across the white board. Documentary news photo, 35mm, harsh on-camera flash, film grain. Accent: deep navy marker strokes against bright white board.

slides.headline: 3) DESCRIBE WHAT YOU WANT. GET WORKING CODE BACK.
slides.body: Software engineers charge $150 an hour to write features like this. Describe the feature in plain words and get complete working code back. Copy-paste prompt: "Write complete working [language] code for this feature: [describe it]. No placeholders, no pseudocode. Add a comment above each function explaining what it does."
slides.image_prompt: Hands typing on a laptop, screen split down the middle: left half holding a single short horizontal chat-line symbol, right half erupting in a cascade of stacked blue code-bracket symbols (zero text), electric blue desk lamp above, dark home office surround. Documentary news photo, 35mm, harsh on-camera flash, film grain. Accent: electric blue code cascade against off-white chat half.

slides.headline: 4) HAVE AI ATTACK ITS OWN CODE BEFORE USERS DO
slides.body: QA engineers charge $100 an hour to find bugs before launch. This prompt has AI act as its own attacker and list every failure point before a single user touches it. Copy-paste prompt: "Act as a senior QA engineer and security tester. Here is my code: [paste it]. List every bug, edge case, and security hole. For each: explain the risk and write the exact fix."

slides.headline: 5) HAND YOUR HARDEST PROBLEM TO AI. WALK AWAY.
slides.body: Senior architects charge $200 an hour for problems like this. Paste the problem in plain words and get a complete fix plan back in minutes, every risk flagged. Copy-paste prompt: "I am building [app type] and stuck on: [describe the problem]. Give me a step-by-step fix plan, list every risk, and write the code I need to implement the solution."

slides.headline: SAVE THIS. YOUR AI DEV TEAM IS 5 PROMPTS LONG.
slides.body: These 5 steps cover every phase a dev team handles. Run them in order and you can ship a real app without hiring a single person. Daily AI news and real skills: @yaffeai

caption:
Swipe through these 5 steps 👇 and you have the complete AI workflow quietly replacing full development teams for business owners who build alone.

Step 1 maps your entire market in 10 minutes with one competitor-analysis prompt, Step 2 turns your raw idea into an ordered task list any AI coding tool can follow, Step 3 gets you working code back just by describing what you want in plain words, Step 4 has AI attack its own code to find every bug before launch, Step 5 hands your hardest technical problem to AI in plain language and gets a complete fix plan back.

A builder with no team can now research, plan, code, test, and fix an entire app in days. The workflow going viral this week proves the job of a 4-person dev team fits in 5 prompts.
